page.layout: One block of running text in a single column, full width. Above it the running head "LIBER IV." and the page number 589. A catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: rem indignissimè abjecturi, divinorum vatum oraculis fidem derogaturi, & pro innata malitia gratiam salutarem in exitium sibi conversuri sint. Quis, inquit, credit auditui nostro: & brachium domini cui revelatum est? Mox tamen causam tanti stuporis exponens, ita eventurum ait, quia tantum ex aspectu & forma externa abjectissima Messiam æstimaturi, nec ad divinam, quam carne obvelatam gerit virtutem, divinaque beneficia per cum humano generi parata penetraturi sint. Ascender[?], inquit, ut surculus coram eo, & ut radix e terra deserta: Non forma ei, nec decor: Despectus & rejectus inter homines, vir dolorum, plenus infirmi-tatis: abscondimus faciem ab eo & nihil reputavimus eum. Tandem universam passionis, mortis, re-surrectionis, gloriæ ac regni Messiæ historiam, quasi in tabella vivis illustratam coloribus brevi-ter proponit. Ad causas etiam harum rerum nos deducit, & fructus ob oculos ponit, triplex scan-dalo remedium opponens: primum quod inno-cens ac sanctus ipse, nostrorum peccatorum rea-tum in se derivaturus, & nostrorum scelerum ex-piationi vitam suam impensurus sit mortemque oppetiturus. Sane, inquit, languores nostros ipse portavit: vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter peccata nostra: Castigatio pacis nostræ super eum: & in livore ejus sanatio nobis. Deinde quod ipse pater cœlestis, filium hoc modo sit contriturus propter peccata nostra: atque istam ejus pœnam in satisfactionem & justitiam impu-taturus credentibus, Jehova, inquit, sic voluit eum conterere: cumq; posuerit ille in sacrificium animam

page.notes: Catchword "suam," printed alone at the lower right, taken out of the text. The first word "rem" is cut off at the left edge of the scan, so the paragraph is marked as a continuation. "Ascender" is uncertain, as the initial letter is ornamented; it may read "Ascendet". "Despectus" is read from a long-s-like form. Hyphens at line ends (re-, brevi-, scan-, inno-, rea-, ex-, infirmi-, impu-) are printed and kept. Italic runs are read from the scan; "inquit" in the "Sane" sentence is taken as italic too.
